$comment: Hand-authored, unlike everything in index/. Each step names the role first and the crate second, because the role is the durable part -- crates get replaced, 'you need argument parsing' does not. `rustgraph.py recipe` resolves every crate named here against the index and marks any that this list does not cover, so a stale or invented name shows up as a failure rather than as confident advice.

recipes.name: cli
recipes.title: Command-line tool
recipes.when: A binary that parses arguments, reads configuration, reports progress and fails with a readable message.

steps.why: Derive-based, and the default the ecosystem converges on.
Application-level errors with context; use thiserror instead when you are writing a library others match on.
Layers file, environment and defaults into one struct.
What Cargo itself uses; least surprising for a Rust tool.
Progress bars and spinners that behave when output is piped.
Library-agnostic; pair with a subscriber in the binary.

recipes.name: web-service
recipes.title: HTTP service
recipes.when: A server exposing JSON endpoints, usually over a database.

steps.why: The runtime the rest of this stack is written against.
Built on hyper and tower by the tokio team; see actix-web for an alternative with its own runtime story.
Underneath axum. Reach for it directly only when you need the lower layer.
Request and response bodies.
Async, compile-time-checked SQL; see sea-orm or diesel if you want an ORM.
Spans survive across await points, which plain log does not.
Cross-platform raw mode, input events and cursor control.
Immediate-mode widgets and layout; renders through crossterm.
A TUI must restore the terminal on the way out, so failures need context.

recipes.name: parser
recipes.title: Parser or data format
recipes.when: Reading a grammar, wire format or domain-specific language.

steps.why: Byte and text parsers built from small combinators; strong on binary formats.
Choose instead of nom when a written PEG grammar is clearer than combinator code.
Once parsed, this is how the value reaches every other format.

recipes.name: data
recipes.title: Data processing
recipes.when: Reading tabular or record data, transforming it, writing it back.

steps.why: Streaming reader and writer with serde integration.
When the work is columnar and would otherwise be pandas.
Turns an iterator chain parallel by changing iter to par_iter.
Intermediates that clean themselves up on drop.
Connection pooling, TLS and JSON in one place.
Required by reqwest's async API; the blocking feature avoids it for simple tools.
Decoding responses.
No dedicated crate in this list; tokio::time is usually enough.

recipes.name: wasm
recipes.title: WebAssembly in the browser
recipes.when: Rust compiled to wasm and called from JavaScript.

steps.why: Generates the bindings in both directions.
The simplest way to pass structured values across the boundary.
